newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS - Atlas Copco sinks after Prime bid.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Atlas Copco sinks after Prime bid.

text.p: Swedish industrial engineer Atlas Copco's shares slid on Tuesday as market players digested news of a $900 million takeover bid for U.S. machinery leaser Prime Service Inc and some brokers lowered their trading suggestions.
"The share appreciated after the announcement but after people went home and did their calculations they decided the price was too high," a Stockholm-based broker said.
At 1300 GMT the share was trading five crowns ($168) lower at 210 crowns, a dip of 2.3 percent on the day, which reversed gains on Monday when the share closed 5.5 crowns higher at 215.

News of Atlas Copco's biggest ever acquisition was unveiled on Monday when the engineer announced a seven billion crown bid for Prime Service. This amounted to $32 a share and represented a 28 percent premium on Prime Service's share price on June 6.
Analysts said the reaction on Tuesday was reminiscent of when Atlas Copco bought Milwaukee Electric Tool Corp for $550 million in 1995.

"It's a high price. Everybody said that when they bought Milwaukee as well but I think there are more positive effects than meet the eye," Handelsbanken engineering analyst Peter Naslund told Reuters.
"There was a high multiple at the time...but they restored the balance sheet pretty quickly after the acquisition.
"In the long term I think we will see synergy effects both on the cost side and the sale side."
But the market was not convinced. Credit ratings agencies reacted quickly to the announcement.
Moody's put Atlas Copco under review for a possible downgrade, saying the all debt-financed bid would increase Atlas Copco's indebtedness by some 1.16 billion crowns.

Standard & Poor's placed Atlas Copco on creditwatch, saying the purchase would increase Atlas Copco's leverage and raise net debt to capital to about 35 percent to 40 percent on a pro forma basis from being cash positive.
Brokerage houses followed suit on Tuesday. Lehman Brothers downgraded its recommendation on Atlas Copco to "neutral" from "outperform" and said it would advise taking profits.
"Our reservations on the financial logic of this acquisition lead us to downgrade our recommendation on the shares, which have already surpassed our 1998 price target," Lehman said.

Atlas Copco said the acquisition, financed through a mixture of cash, commercial paper and banklines, would boost cash flow but the deal would dilute earnings per share by up to five percent in the first two years.

Paribas engineering analyst Christian Diebitsch said it was arguable whether the two companies had much products overlap with only 20 percent of Prime's products coinciding with Atlas Copco's existing range.

"People had been buying the share because it's a very focused company and if they now start to acquire sizeable entities only marginally related to its core business, this might dilute that focus," Diebitsch said.
Atlas Copco's share price has risen almost 30 percent since the end of 1996.
In light of the stock's strong performance this year, Diebitsch said he had revised his recommendation on the share after the purchase of Prime Service to sell from hold.
Other analysts also said this bull run may be over.
"I am positive towards the acquistion of Prime Service but negative towards Atlas Copco. The share price has rallied in 1997," one Stockholm based analyst said.
"The share could have been going up because of rumours about this deal and now that people see the details it is falling off a bit."
-- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1003 ($ = 7.757 Swedish Crowns)
